source.section: Schedule 2 line 11 code 632 and PDF page 22 Military Retirement Income and/or Survivor's Benefits Deduction; Schedule 2 lines 5 and 6 (PDF page 17 Lines 5 and 6: 'Indiana does not tax Social Security income or the railroad retirement benefits'); Schedule 3 line 1 (PDF page 24: joint 2,000, all other filers 1,000), line 4 (PDF page 25: 1,000 age 65 or older), line 5 (PDF page 25: 500 age 65 or older and IT-40 line 1 under 40,000, or under 20,000 married filing separately); Form IT-40 lines 1-8 (PDF page 1; line 8 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'); booklet PDF page 8 Line 1; PDF pages 5-6 rounding

worked: Federal AGI = military retirement person 0 25,000.00 + taxable Social Security 9,600.00 = 34,600.00. Social Security received: person 0 30,000.00; the federal taxable amount from the federal worksheet is 9,600.00. Federal taxable income = 34,600.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 16,850.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Indiana starts from federal AGI). Form IT-40 line 1 federal AGI 34,600.00. Line 2 add-backs 0.00; line 3 = 34,600.00 + 0.00 = 34,600.00. Schedule 2: line 5 taxable Social Security 9,600.00; line 11 code 632 military retirement 25,000.00; line 12 total = 34,600.00. IT-40 line 4 = 34,600.00. Line 5 = 34,600.00 - 34,600.00 = 0.00. Schedule 3: line 1 1,000.00; line 4 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00; line 5 IT-40 line 1 34,600.00 is under 40,000.00: 1 x 500.00 = 500.00; line 7 total = 2,500.00. IT-40 line 6 = 2,500.00. Line 7 = 0.00 - 2,500.00 = -2,500.00; the form allows the negative figure and line 8 is left blank; taxable income is floored at 0.00. Line 8 = 0.00 x 0.03 = 0.00. No credits; county tax (line 9) is local and out of scope. State income tax 0.00. Federal AGI is over 10,000, so the Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly is not in play.
